title: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
name: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
metaTitle: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Sourcing single-tenant net lease replacement candidates around Fort Worth with lease abstract review, guaranty verification, and ground lease diligence.

sections.html: A single-tenant net lease property is only as reliable as the lease document backing it, and a Fort Worth pad site advertised at a headline cap rate can still carry a guaranty, reimbursement structure, or reversion clause that changes the real return once the lease abstract is reviewed line by line.

sections.heading: Where STNL Development Is Concentrated Around Fort Worth
sections.html: New single-tenant retail and quick-service pads have followed rooftop growth along the corridors feeding the Alliance industrial and logistics development, where warehouse and air-cargo employment has pulled in new residential subdivisions and the retail pads that typically trail them. Established corridors closer to downtown and the Cultural District carry older net lease stock with different lease vintages and rent structures, and we source across both rather than defaulting to whichever segment has the most current listings.

sections.heading: Corporate Guaranty and Lease Abstract Review
sections.html:
A corporate guaranty from a national tenant is not automatically stronger than a franchisee guaranty, and we pull the actual guaranty language rather than relying on a broker's description of the tenant as corporate or investment grade. Some national brands lease through single-purpose franchisee entities with limited balance sheets even when the marketing materials imply direct corporate backing.

Reimbursement structure matters just as much: an absolute net lease places roof and structure obligations on the tenant, while a double-net lease can leave the landlord holding capital exposure the headline cap rate never priced in.

Corporate guaranty language also needs to specify which entity in a franchise system stands behind the rent obligation, since a guaranty running only to a regional franchisee holding company carries different recovery prospects in a default than one running to the parent brand itself. We request the guarantor's corporate structure alongside the guaranty document rather than treating a brand name on the storefront as proof of the guaranty behind it.

sections.heading: Documentation Requested Before an STNL Property Is Identified
sections.html:
Before a net lease property is placed on a 45-day identification list, we assemble the records needed to confirm the lease performs as advertised.

  • full lease abstract, including reimbursement structure and roof and structure responsibility
  • guaranty document and corporate structure of the guarantor entity
  • rent escalation schedule for the full remaining term and any option periods
  • estoppel certificate request drafted for execution before closing
  • site plan confirming reciprocal easement and parking obligations tied to any outparcel

sections.heading: Ground Lease and Reversion Considerations
sections.html:
Some Fort Worth pad sites are structured as ground leases rather than fee-simple sales, and a ground lease replacement property carries a different risk profile: the investor owns the land under the tenant's building but not the building itself, with a reversion clause governing what happens at lease expiration. We confirm whether a candidate is fee-simple or ground lease before it goes on an identification list, since the two structures are not interchangeable for exchange purposes despite similar cap rates.

The remaining ground lease term matters as much as the reversion clause itself, since a ground lease with fifteen years remaining behaves differently as a replacement candidate than one with fifty years remaining and multiple renewal options still available to the tenant. We confirm the full remaining term, rather than only the current lease period, before comparing a ground lease candidate against a fee-simple alternative on cap rate alone.

sections.heading: Cap Rate Discipline Against 45-Day Deadlines
sections.html: Net lease inventory moves quickly once a listing hits the market, and the pressure of an approaching 45-day deadline can push an investor toward a marginal cap rate simply because the paperwork is clean and available. We hold the same lease and guaranty standards regardless of how many days remain in the identification window, since a weak tenant credit does not improve because the deadline is close.

faqs.q: Is a franchisee guaranty weaker than a corporate guaranty on a net lease property?
faqs.a: Not automatically, but it needs to be verified rather than assumed, since some national brands lease through single-purpose franchisee entities with limited balance sheets even when marketing materials describe the tenant as investment grade.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an absolute net lease and a double-net lease for replacement sourcing?
faqs.a: An absolute net lease places roof and structure responsibility on the tenant, while a double-net lease can leave the landlord holding that capital exposure, which changes the real return behind a headline cap rate.

faqs.q: How does a ground lease replacement property differ from a fee-simple purchase?
faqs.a: In a ground lease the investor owns the land under the tenant's building rather than the building itself, and a reversion clause governs what happens at lease expiration, making the two structures unsuitable to compare on cap rate alone.

faqs.q: Why is rooftop growth near the Alliance corridor relevant to net lease sourcing?
faqs.a: Warehouse and air-cargo employment growth in that corridor has pulled in new residential subdivisions, and new single-tenant retail and quick-service pads typically follow that rooftop growth, creating a distinct supply pipeline from older corridors closer to downtown.

faqs.q: Should lease and guaranty standards change when a 45-day deadline is approaching?
faqs.a: No, the same lease abstract and guaranty review standards apply regardless of days remaining in the identification window, since a weak tenant credit does not improve under time pressure.

faqs.q: Why does the remaining term on a ground lease matter beyond the reversion clause itself?
faqs.a: A ground lease with fifteen years remaining behaves very differently as a replacement candidate than one with fifty years and multiple renewal options, so the full remaining term needs to be confirmed before comparing it against a fee-simple alternative.
